description: In response to growing regional disparities in AI infrastructure investment and repeated incidents affecting southern and eastern member states, a coalition of mid-sized EU countries forms an informal mutual aid pact for cyber and AI incident response. The pact includes shared rapid-response teams, joint simulations, and pooled reserve compute for crisis deployment, operating outside formal EU structures but with tacit Commission approval. It emerges as a workaround to slow central coordination and signals growing fragmentation in implementation despite unity in policy.
